::: notes
"If you dozed off, this is the slide to wake up for. Adopt datom and this is what you get, every time."

1:15.

Then the frame: "These aren't eight features. They're consequences of one decision: data as code." Each one falls out of the split you saw two slides back: the values in storage, the record in git.

Read them plainly, one breath each:

- Nothing is overwritten. Every version stays readable, forever.
- Same values, same hash, on any machine. Identity doesn't depend on a path.
- Every table knows its parents, at exact versions, and the code that made it.
- A set pins exact versions, and it moves only when you release it.
- Every write is a commit: attributed, reviewable, and recoverable. Pull before push; if something goes wrong it fails loudly, and repairs from git.
- Readers need storage only: no git, no token.
- Nothing to host: no server, no database. It fits inside the SCE you already run.
- An open format: parquet and JSON, readable from any language. No lock-in, not even to datom.

Then straight into the limits: "And here's what it isn't. Yet."
:::
